about: The Xbox 360 avatar API of the FH2MP LSP for Encore: native/internal/lsp/avatar.go and native/internal/avatars.

TestAvatarContract (native/internal/lsp/avatar_test.go) writes this file with FH2MP_WRITE_AVATAR_CONTRACT=1 and fails when the server no longer answers what it says. Encore keeps a copy in testdata/ and its interop lane checks the copy against FH2MP at proto/FH2MP_COMMIT.
Base64 is the standard alphabet with padding (RFC 4648 section 4), checked strictly.

Errors are {"error": <code>, "message": <text>} with the HTTP status. The code is for programs, the message for people. A request whose Content-Length is over the route's limit gets 413 {"error": "too_large"} before it is read.
There is no store and no money: avatar items are rewards (later The Eliminator's battle pass), granted by the server only.

limits.coloursLines: each line "<record> <palette>": two numbers of 1 to 6 digits, one space, ended by "\n"; "" or no colours field = no choices
limits.bodyFormat: PNG, 8 bits per channel, grey, grey+alpha, RGB or RGBA, not interlaced; width and height each 64 to 1024 pixels; at most 2000000 bytes as sent
limits.bodyServed: the server keeps and serves its own encoding of the pixels (pngtool), never the uploaded bytes: compare pictures by their pixels

itemId.text: 32 lowercase hex digits: the item's 16 id bytes in the order the manifest holds them. The server reads either case and answers in lower case.
itemId.empty: 16 zero bytes are an empty slot, not an item (nor can they be granted).

slots.what: face parts: chin, nose and ears (16 bytes each), then six 32-byte face textures (mouth, eyes, eyebrows, facial hair, eye shadow, facial features); read as fifteen 16-byte slots, so a texture's second half is read too
asset entries, the id in each entry's first 16 bytes: body, head, 13 worn items, 7 of the basic outfit (to 0x3E0)

itemId.worn: A manifest wears every non-empty id in those slots. Nothing else in it is read as an id.
itemId.rewards: The reward catalog lists the items that must be owned to be worn; every other item is free. It holds 0 items in this build (none yet: the battle pass picks them). PUT refuses a manifest wearing a catalog item the account does not own.

card: Every community card (GET /v1/community, /v1/community/player/<xuid>, invites, ...) carries avatarVersion next to gamerpicVersion: the time of the avatar's last save in seconds since 1970 (a float), above the one before at every save; 0 = no avatar. Fetch GET /v1/avatar/<xuid> again when it changes.
grants: Items are granted by the server only: avatars.Store.Grant(xuid, item, source) (the battle pass calls it later). No client request grants.

For tests, the operators' control line (loopback only, like every /admin/ endpoint) answers one text line: GET /admin/avatar-items?xuid=<xuid>&grant=<item>[&source=<source>] grants (source "admin" when left out) and answers "granted <item> to <xuid hex> (source <source>)", "<xuid hex> already owns <item>" or "refused: <reason>"; GET /admin/avatar-items?xuid=<xuid> lists "<item> granted <time> by <source>" per item. xuid is decimal or 0x hex; source is 1 to 64 of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -.
An account keeps its items when it deletes its avatar.

about: The steps run in order on one empty database, with these accounts signed in, and the reward catalog holding the items in rewards (the shipped catalog is empty).
clock is the server's time from that step on, in seconds since 1970: versions and grant times come from it. A step with repeat is sent that many times, each answered alike.

control is an operators' control line and answer its text. pick: the answer has more fields than these, and the contract pins only the ones listed. png: the picture's size and the SHA-256 of its decoded pixel rows (width x channels bytes each, top row first).
